items.title: Supreme Court dismisses review petition in Ujjain Takiya Masjid demolition case
items.summary: The Supreme Court has dismissed a petition seeking review of its November 7, 2025 order rejecting a challenge concerning the demolition of the Takiya Masjid in Ujjain. [Mohammed Taiyab v. State of Madhya Pradesh & Ors.] A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta found no apparent error warranting reconsideration of its earlier order. It also rejected the request for an open-court hearing. “We have perused the review petition as well as the grounds in support thereof and are convinced that the order dated 07.11.2025, of which review has been sought, does not suffer from any error apparent warranting its reconsideration,” the Court said in its November 17 order. The original plea was filed by thirteen residents who used to offer namaz at the mosque. They alleged that the Madhya Pradesh government demolished the 200-year-old mosque to expand the parking area for the adjoining Mahakal Temple complex. Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta According to the petitioners, the mosque was notified as waqf property in 1985 and remained in use until it was demolished in January 2025. They alleged that the demolition violated the Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act, 1991, the Waqf Act, 1995, and the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013. The petitioners also alleged irregularities in the land acquisition process, claiming that compensation was paid to unauthorised occupants and encroachers to create a false basis for the acquisition. Seeking restoration of the mosque, they approached the Madhya Pradesh High Court. A single judge dismissed their plea, and a Division Bench later rejected their appeal. Their challenge before the Supreme Court was dismissed on November 7, 2025. They then sought a review of that order, which the top court rejected on November 17. Advocates Vaibhav Choudhary, Mayank Singh Rawat, Zaid Ahmed and Ashhar Warsi appeared for the petitioner. [Read Order]

items.title: Air India crash probe nearing completion: Centre tells Supreme Court
items.summary: The Central government informed the Supreme Court on Thursday that the investigation into the June 2025 Air India plane crash in Ahmedabad, which claimed 260 lives, was nearing completion. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing petitions seeking an independent investigation into the crash, including pleas filed by the father of one of the deceased pilots and an aviation safety organisation. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta , appearing for the Centre, sought an adjournment of two to three weeks to allow investigators to complete the process. "We are at the fag end of the investigation," Mehta submitted. He maintained that the delay was not intentional and explained that aviation accident investigations have to comply with international protocols. Advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing for one of the petitioners, opposed the adjournment and pointed out that the final investigation report has not yet been released. Bhushan referred to the Centre's affidavit indicating that the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) expected to prepare its draft final report by the first week of October. However, the Court accepted the Centre's request for additional time and directed that the petitions be listed after two weeks. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana The London-bound Boeing 787 Dreamliner crashed into the BJ Medical College hostel complex on June 12, 2025 less than a minute after taking off from Ahmedabad, killing 241 of the 242 people on board and 19 others on the ground. The petitioners moved the Court contending that an incomplete or prejudiced inquiry would endanger future passengers and undermine aviation safety. They also questioned the AAIB's preliminary investigation report for allegedly focusing on pilot actions without conclusive evidence. The petition by Pushkaraj Sabharwal, the father of deceased pilot Captain Sumeet Sabharwal, and the Federation of Indian Pilots was filed seeking formation of an independent committee , headed by a retired Supreme Court judge, to conduct a "fair, transparent and technically robust" investigation into the crash. Another petition was filed by Safety Matters Foundation seeking an independent inquiry into the accident. The AAIB's preliminary report recorded that the aircraft's engine fuel-control switches had moved from the run position to cutoff shortly after takeoff. items.title: Taj Trapezium Zone: Supreme Court orders fresh meeting of CEC and TTZ body after internal discord over manufacturing cluster
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Central Empowered Committee (CEC) and the Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ) Authority to hold a fresh meeting regarding the proposed Integrated Manufacturing Cluster in Agra near the Taj Mahal. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued the direction after being informed of an internal disagreement over the clearance earlier granted to the proposed industrial project within the 10,400 sq. km eco-sensitive zone. "It seems to us that there is a necessity to hold a fresh meeting between the TTZ authority and the CEC to iron out the glitches and submit a joint comprehensive report. Let the meeting be held, the conditions discussed, and a joint report be submitted within two weeks," the Court ordered. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana The representatives of the CEC and the TTZ Authority had met on September 22 and decided to grant conditional permission for the project. However, the Court noted that a CEC member AK Mohanty sent an email on November 6, expressing reservations about the decision purportedly reached at the September meeting. Attorney General R Venkataramani Attorney General R Venkataramani submitted that while the CEC had recommended conditional tree-felling permission, the minutes of the meeting were not properly circulated. He suggested that both bodies meet again to resolve any differences and report back to the Court. Industrial activity and tree felling within the Taj Trapezium Zone spread across 10,400 sq. km around the Taj Mahal and other heritage monuments are strictly regulated under Supreme Court supervision to prevent environmental degradation. In July 2026, the Supreme Court allowed the TTZ Authority to process around 400 pending applications for setting up non-polluting micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs). It clarified that the authorities can proceed without the Court's prior leave only when the TTZ Authority and nominated experts from the CEC and NEERI are unanimous. items.title: BCI asks law aspirants to verify authenticity and approval of institutions before admission
items.summary: The Bar Council of India (BCI) has issued an advisory asking law aspirants to independently verify institutions’ authenticity and BCI approval status before taking admission. The advisory, issued on November 19, complies with the Supreme Court’s October 9 order in Ayesha Jain v. Amity University . The Court had directed the University Grants Commission (UGC) and all regulators to caution students against dealing with institutions without first verifying their authenticity. BCI has advised students to ensure that the institution is legally authorised to impart the concerned law degree course and that the law degree satisfies the applicable requirements for recognition by the BCI for the purposes of enrolment as an advocate. It has clarified that mere establishment of a university, grant of permission or no-objection certificate by a state government, or grant of affiliation by a university does not, by itself, dispense with the requirement of approval by BCI under the Rules of Legal Education, 2008. The list of approved institutions and courses is available on BCI's website. BCI has also advised that prospective students should specifically ascertain whether the concerned institution possesses valid approval for the three-year LL.B. course or five-year integrated law degree course and whether the number of sections and sanctioned student intake correspond to the approval granted by BCI. "Approval granted for one programme, academic session, section or intake should not be presumed to extend automatically to another programme, session, section or intake," the advisory states. NLSIU, TNNLU still not on BCI's approved list of law colleges as deadline lapses again; GNLU secures approval Universities, law colleges and admission agencies have been cautioned against misleading representations on approval status. A pending application, inspection or proposal shall not be represented as the grant of approval, BCI has said. It has further said that universities and centres of legal education (CLEs) must make accurate particulars on approval and intake readily available and provide approval documents on request. Where approval is conditional, they must not conceal or misrepresent any material limitation. BCI has clarified that admission without the requisite approval may have serious implications for the recognition of the qualification for enrolment as an advocate. items.title: Supreme Court reserves judgment on plea to raise retirement age of district judges to 62 years
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday reserved its judgment on whether the retirement age of district judges across the country should be increased from 60 to 62 years [All India Judges Association v. Union of India] . A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing the long-pending All India Judges Association case concerning service conditions of judicial officers. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, CJI Surya Kant and Justice V Mohana During the hearing, Senior Advocate Siddharth Bhatnagar , assisting the Court as amicus curiae , informed the Bench that 15 States and Union Territories had supported the proposal, while 12 continued to oppose it. Four others - including Delhi, Gujarat, Jharkhand and Puducherry - sought additional time. Senior Advocate Siddharth Bhatnagar The Court asked Attorney General R Venkataramani to make a final attempt to persuade the opposing States, particularly Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, to reconsider their stand within two weeks. Attorney General R Venkataramani The Bench also questioned the financial burden cited by certain States, observing that retaining experienced judicial officers could reduce the immediate expenditure associated with retirement benefits and fresh appointments. Justice Bagchi noted that judicial vacancies were already substantial and questioned whether extending the tenure of serving judges would adversely affect recruitment opportunities. CJI Surya Kant emphasised the importance of retaining experienced officers while acknowledging the need to induct younger judges into the judiciary. Senior Advocate Vijay Hansaria supported a uniform increase in retirement age, while Senior Advocate Vikas Singh opposed making continued service beyond 60 conditional upon mandatory suitability assessments by the respective High Courts. Senior Advocate Vijay Hansaria Senior Advocate Vikas Singh The issue has been under consideration for several years. In September this year, the Supreme Court directed seven consenting States, including Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal, to amend their service rules to permit eligible district judges to continue until 62, subject to suitability and performance assessments. The proposal also draws upon recommendations made by the Justice K Jagannatha Shetty Commission concerning judicial service conditions. The Court has now reserved its decision on the larger issue of uniform retirement age.

items.title: Supreme Court quashes Odisha's 2021 land acquisition for Dalmia Cement mining project
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday set aside the State of Odisha’s acquisition of land in three villages in Sundargarh district for a Dalmia Cement mining project. [Bibol Toppo v. Odisha] A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma held that the State proceeded without obtaining the mandatory consent of the gram sabhas and affected families. It overturned the Orissa High Court’s September 2024 judgment upholding the acquisition. It further said that the High Court’s treatment of gram sabha consent had “the effect of reducing a mandatory statutory requirement into a paper formality.” “ Far from a meaningful consent, there is not even paper consent of Gram Sabha in this case, ” the Court said, noting that both gram sabhas had rejected the proposal in January 2020. Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Satish Chandra Sharma Dalmia Cement already held a mining lease extending to 2040. In 2015, it asked the Odisha government to acquire surface rights over agricultural land in Kukuda, Bihabandha and Lanjiberna so it could expand mining operations. The State went ahead with the acquisition despite the resolutions rejecting it. Residents of the three villages challenged the proceedings. The High Court had held that the requirement of consent from 80 per cent of affected families did not apply because title to the land would vest in the State. It also held that even if such consent was required, it could be gathered at different stages of the acquisition. The Supreme Court held that the purpose of the acquisition determined which safeguards applied. The land was sought exclusively for mining by a private company. Section 2(2)(b) of the 2013 land acquisition law, therefore, required the consent of at least 80 per cent of affected families during the social impact assessment, before the State examined the proposal. Consent obtained at a later stage could not cure the defect. The Bench held that Section 41(3) imposed a separate requirement of prior gram sabha consent because the land fell within a Scheduled Area under the Fifth Schedule to the Constitution. The requirement applied even to urgent acquisitions. The Court also found no evidence that the mandatory public hearing on the draft social impact assessment had taken place. items.title: Calcutta High Court closes plea for probe into death of student who died after drinking extremely hot tea
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Thursday declined to entertain a plea seeking directions for an independent, impartial and transparent investigation into the death of a class 12 student after he drank scalding hot tea at his school's canteen [ Manaranjan Mahata v. State of West Bengal ]. The petition had been filed by Manaranjan Mahata (petitioner), the father of the deceased boy, who was a student of a school run by the Ramkrishna Mission at Narendrapur, Kolkata. Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya who heard the matter, noted that the student had died on June 30, 2026 and that a charge sheet has already been filed after a criminal investigation by the police. The High Court, therefore, was not inclined to issue further directions. Justice Bhattacharyya, however, clarified that the petitioner was at liberty to seek further police investigation under Section 193 (9) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, into the circumstances surrounding his son's death. "Chargesheet dated 9th September, 2026 is filed on concluding investigation. If petitioner (the father) is dissatisfied with the manner of investigation and chargesheet filed, on conclusion of such investigation, in that event, he has remedy under Section 193 (9) of the BNSS, 2023 by approaching jurisdictional magistrate seeking further investigation," the Court observed. Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya In his plea, Mahata had primarily prayed for a direction upon the police to conduct an impartial and transparent investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death of his boy and for the appointment of a retired Judge to monitor the investigation. According to the plea, the school authorities were aware that the boy was showing signs of illness soon after drinking the hot tea. Mahata claimed that they contacted him at a belated stage, several hours after the incident when the condition of the boy had already transitioned from bad to worse. It was also alleged that timely medical attention was not provided to the boy at the school premises, which further worsened his condition. A subsequent post-mortem report showed that the boy succumbed to asphyxia resulting from laryngeal oedema, following thermal injury to the upper respiratory and upper gastro-oesophageal tract. The plea also underscored that the CCTV footage recording of the events leading up to the boy's death had not been adequately preserved. items.title: Ship can't be arrested to recover wages of another vessel's crew under same management: Kerala High Court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday held that a ship cannot be arrested to recover crew wages relating to another vessel merely because they are managed by the same shipping company [ Light House Marine Service India Pvt Ltd v Charter and Parties interested in the Vessel MT Ocean Faye & ors ]. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar VM observed that a vessel could be arrested in such circumstances only if, prima facie, there was a commonality of interest between the shipowners, along with a clear intention to defraud a creditor. Merely because the vessels were managed by the same entity did not mean that the entity also owned them, the Court pointed out. The Court made the observation while dismissing an appeal filed by a manning agent (crew-supply agent) named Light House Marine Service India Pvt Lt. Light House Marine Service (appellant) had sought to arrest the vessel MT Ocean Faye to recover wages it had paid to crew members of three other vessels, all of which are managed by Star Voyages Shipping Services LLC. The Court held that such a contractual dispute between a crew-supplying agency and a ship manager over the dues paid to the crew of certain vessels cannot justify the arrest of another vessel, merely because all the vessels involved had a common manager. " The appellant is neither a bareboat charterer nor a demise charterer and is only a manning agent or crew supplier who claims to have entered into an agreement to supply crew to the vessels managed by the second defendant. A manning agent who has a contractual arrangement with Ship’s Manager does not stand on similar footing as a demise charter or bareboat charter qua the owner of the vessel. He is far distanced from the shipowner and his vessel and cannot, in law, aspire to arrest the vessel for his disputes and claims with the Ship’s Manager... The crucial test of ownership has not been established in the instant case," the Court held. Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar VM (Kerala HC) The appellant had claimed that it paid the wages of crew members aboard three vessels, namely MT Eastern Pearl, MT Fast Kathy and MT Sea Fidelity, after Star Voyages failed to make these payments despite contractual obligations to do so. Later, Star Voyages also failed to reimburse the amount despite repeated demands by the appellant. items.title: NCLT declines to revive Essar Group's OGD Services despite settlement of financial debts
items.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) at Mumbai has dismissed an application filed by Essar Shipping Limited seeking to revive OGD Services Limited, an Essar Group company undergoing liquidation, despite the settlement of its financial debts with Punjab National Bank (PNB) and Union Bank of India (UBI). A Bench comprising judicial member KR Saji Kumar and technical member Anil Raj Chellan held that the tribunal’s inherent powers cannot be exercised to permit withdrawal of liquidation proceedings in the absence of an express statutory provision. “The inherent power of the tribunal cannot be exercised to permit a withdrawal during the liquidation process, thereby conferring substantive rights on persons who would otherwise not be eligible to submit a resolution plan,” the bench held. PNB had initiated insolvency proceedings against OGD Services under Section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC). The NCLT admitted the company into the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) in February 2023. After no compliant resolution plan was received, the Committee of Creditors (CoC), comprising PNB and UBI, unanimously decided to liquidate the company. A liquidation order was passed thereafter. Subsequently, Essar Shipping, the holding company and corporate guarantor of OGD Services, settled the financial creditors' dues. It then approached NCLT seeking recall of the liquidation order and revival of OGD Services as a going concern. The tribunal noted that while Section 12A of the IBC provides a mechanism for withdrawal of insolvency proceedings after admission, there is no corresponding provision permitting withdrawal once liquidation has begun. The NCLT also took note of the October 14, 2025 amendment to the IBBI (Liquidation Process) Regulations, 2016, which removed the provision relating to the sale of a corporate debtor as a going concern in cases where such a sale had not already commenced. “The recent legislative changes also fail to indicate a preference for preserving the corporate debtor as a going concern, even at the risk of losing the value of intangible assets and a substantial reduction in the realisation,” the bench said. Relying on the Supreme Court's decision in Ebix Singapore (P) Ltd. v. items.title: Will examine whether case on private university audit needs to continue: Supreme Court after Bench change
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday indicated that it will examine in January whether to continue hearing the public interest litigation (PIL) in which a Bench led by Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah had earlier issued sweeping directions for the audit of private universities across India [ Ayesha Jain v. Amity University Noida & Ors ]. The development comes days after the case was shifted from the Justice Amanullah bench to a three-judge bench comprising Justice Vikram Nath , R Mahadevan and Aparesh Kumar Singh . "What we propose is we fix the matter for January. We will consider the grievance of the petitioner, subject to report of Mr. Prasad (Mr. Ashok Prasad, who had been tasked with enquiring into certain allegations made by the petitioner regarding Amity University). University has already filed its counter. We will decide then what is the scope of the PIL. Whether to continue it further or not, " the new bench said today. The Court then proceeded to adjourn the case till January 2027. "Let this matter be listed on Jan 11. The further issues raised in this matter would be considered on the next date... We will consider whether to entertain this petition or not or how far we will carry this , " today's order records. Justice Vikram Nath, Justice R Mahadevan and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh The case before the Court originally began in mid-2025 as an individual grievance filed by 23-year-old student Ayesha Jain against Amity University, Noida. Jain alleged that University officials harassed her, barred her from classes and caused her to lose an academic year after she legally changed her name from Khushi Jain to Ayesha Jain. While the Bench pulled up Amity's top officials over their treatment of the student, it refused to close the matter after granting her relief. Instead, in November 2025, A Bench of Justices Amanullah and NV Anjaria expanded the scope of the petition in the larger public interest to scrutinise how private universities across India are established, funded and regulated. Over the course of multiple hearings, the Bench issued a string of far-reaching directives, including those to furnish details of how private universities are set up and governed, directions to curb profiteering and measures to crack down on fake colleges . items.title: Ariyil Shukoor murder: Kerala court acquits CPI(M) leader P Jayarajan and 17 others, convicts 13
items.summary: A Special Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) court in Ernakulam on Thursday (November 19) convicted 13 persons and acquitted 18 persons, including Communist Party of India (Marxist) leaders P Jayarajan and TV Rajesh, in the 2012 Ariyil Shukoor murder case [ State of Kerala v Sumesh KV & ors ]. Shyamjith, son of CPI(M) State Secretary MV Govindan, is among those acquitted in the case. Special CBI court III Judge Sabarinathan P pronounced the verdict while sentencing seven convicts to life imprisonment. Of the 13 persons convicted, 7 were found guilty of murder, 5 were convicted of offences relating to trespass, wrongful restraint and criminal intimidation, while 1 was found guilty of destroying evidence connected to the crime. The 7 convicts found guilty of murder - namely KV Sumeesh (A1) Anoop (A3), Pavithran (A7), Manoharan (A9), MV Dineshan (A10), Bijumon (A12) and Shijin Mohan (A15) - have been sentenced to life imprisonment. The case concerns the murder of Muslim Students Federation (MSF) worker Abdul Shukoor in Kannur. According to the prosecution, Shukoor was killed on February 20, 2012, in retaliation to an attack on a vehicle carrying Jayarajan and Rajesh earlier that day. The CBI alleged that the murder was planned at the Taliparamba Co-operative Hospital, where the two CPI(M) leaders had been admitted following the attack on their convoy. It was further alleged that Shukoor and his companions were detained for nearly two and a half hours and that Shukoor was identified through photographs shared over mobile phones before he was killed at Keezhara in Kannur. The Kerala Police initially investigated the case. However, following a petition filed by Shukoor mother, the Kerala High Court ordered a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe in February 2016. The CBI filed its chargesheet in February 2019 and the murder trial began in May 2025, during which around 41 witnesses were examined. The charges framed in the case included various provisions of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC), including Sections 302 (murder), 307 (attempt to murder), 120B (criminal conspiracy), 364 (kidnapping or abducting in order to murder), 201 (causing disappearance of evidence) and 149 (offences committed in prosecution of the common object of an unlawful assembly), among others. items.title: Independent directors: A protective mechanism or a false sense of security?
items.summary: During a recent board meeting, a significant related party transaction was scrutinized and subsequently approved. Two years later, this transaction is now subject to investigation by regulatory authorities. Independent directors often perceive Section 149(12) of the Companies Act, 2013 as a safeguard against personal liability. As they are typically not involved in the management or daily operations of the company, this provision limits their liability to matters they were aware of through Board discussions that they either supported or contributed to or in cases where their due diligence was insufficient. However, the necessity for diligence fundamentally alters the interpretation of this provision; it necessitates tangible evidence of actions taken rather than merely serving an honorary capacity upon appointment. Defining what an “independent” director entails According to Section 149(6) of the Companies Act, 2013, a director qualifies as independent if they are neither managing nor nominee directors and if the board assesses them as honest with adequate experience and no ties to either the company or its promoters. For publicly traded companies, at least one-third of directors must be independent (Section 149(4)), which increases to fifty percent under Regulation 17(1)(b) of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 (“LODR”) when there is no regular non-executive chairperson affiliated with promoters. Expectations from independent directors The Code outlined in Schedule IV requires independent directors to provide external perspectives during board deliberations while ensuring that management is held accountable for decisions impacting minority shareholders' interests, effectively and thoroughly evaluating transactions involving related parties. This Code delineates significant responsibilities; failure to meet these obligations could jeopardize a director's ability to assert due diligence later on. items.title: Supreme Court orders constitution of panels of lawyers, sign language interpreters to assist disabled advocates
items.summary: The Supreme Court will set up a permanent committee to address issues concerning the rights of disabled persons, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant announced on Wednesday. CJI Kant also directed the Supreme Court Legal Services Committee to constitute panels of young lawyers and sign language interpreters to assist advocates with disabilities during proceedings before the Court. The announcements were made during a meeting between CJI Kant and Heba Hagrass , the United Nations' Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities at the Supreme Court. Lawyers with disabilities and representatives of civil society also attended the meeting. During the interaction, CJI Kant observed that ensuring the rights of disabled persons is a constitutional obligation and that equality is a fundamental principle of the Constitution. He stressed the need to identify gaps in the implementation of laws and government schemes to ensure that persons with disabilities could exercise their rights in practice. Referring to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, CJI Kant acknowledged the steps taken by the government and the judiciary over the past decade. CJI Kant said that courts could step in when administrative delays prevent persons with disabilities from getting benefits under laws and government schemes. They could direct public authorities to perform their duties and monitor whether those directions were followed. He also highlighted the role of public interest litigation in helping persons with disabilities enforce their rights. CJI Kant referred to Article 142 of the Constitution, which empowers the Supreme Court to pass orders necessary to do complete justice in cases before it. He encouraged the UN officials present to share India's experience in protecting disability rights with other countries. Speaking about steps taken within the judiciary, he referred to reservation for disabled persons in judicial services and the relaxation of qualifying marks for eligible candidates with disabilities. He also encouraged courts across the country to share practices that have helped improve accessibility and inclusion. Officials from the UN human rights office and the UN Resident Coordinator's office in India attended the meeting, along with representatives of Saksham Trust, iProbono, Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy, the Politics and Disability Forum and Mission Accessibility. items.title: Kerala High Court upholds injunction against candy maker over Kandamkulathy Vaidyasala's 'ELADI' mark
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently upheld an interim injunction restraining Thrissur based Ameya Sweets from using the trademarks 'ELADI' and 'ELADI THRILL' for its candies after finding that the marks were deceptively similar to the registered 'ELADI' trademark of Kandamkulathy Vaidyasala. [Mrs Vineetha Suresh Babu & anr v Dr Rose Mary Wilson & ors] A Division Bench of Chief Justice Soumen Sen and Justice Syam Kumar VM on November 12, dismissed an appeal filed by Ameya Sweets and its proprietor Vineetha Suresh Babu, against an order of the Additional District Court, Thrissur. The Court observed that Kandamkulathy Vaidyasala had established that the world 'ELADI' had become closely associated with its products through decades of use. items.title: Maharashtra court staff temporarily suspend strike after Bombay High Court intervention
items.summary: Employees across all district and magistrate courts in Maharashtra have temporarily suspended their indefinite strike , which commenced on November 17 over demands for a revised pay hike. The decision to halt the statewide agitation came after an online meeting held on Wednesday with an administrative committee of Bombay High Court judges. A joint communication announcing halt on strike was issued by the Maharashtra State Court Employees Sanghatana (Class-C), the Maharashtra State Judicial Stenographers Association, the State Judicial Bailiffs Employees Sanghantana, and the Class-D Employees Sanghatana on Wednesday. According to the official communication addressed to the Registrar General of the Bombay High Court, the virtual meeting took place in the afternoon today. In Mumbai, the meeting was attended by administrative judges, Justices AS Gadkari , GS Kulkarni , BP Colabawalla and Suman Shyam led by the Chief Justice Mahesh Chandra Tripathi . A communication from the High Court clarified that the senior-most judges of the benches at Nagpur, Aurangabad and the circuit bench at Kolhapur also participated in the deliberations. The office-bearers stated that they are putting the strike on hold to honor the direct request and assurances made by the judges and to ensure uninterrupted administration of justice across the State's judicial system. The associations said that the final resolution of the dispute now hinges on upcoming talks with the State government. The employee associations have been assured an official meeting with the Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on November 26. Despite this temporary reprieve, the associations made it clear that the strike has not been permanently called off. They have warned that if a satisfactory resolution is not achieved or a concrete Government Resolution (GR) regarding their long-pending demands is not issued by November 26, they reserve the right to resume the agitation. Nearly 34,000 Maharashtra subordinate court staff began an indefinite strike on November 17, disrupting judicial work. Protesting staffers staged demonstrations outside several civil and sessions courts outside court complexes as the agitation got underway. The employees are protesting the State government's ongoing failure to implement a proposed wage increment based firmly on the principle of "equal pay for equal work". items.title: Foreigners accused of visa overstay can't be kept in detention centres after getting bail: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has ruled that foreign nationals accused of overstaying their visas cannot be directed to remain in detention centres as a condition for being granted bail. A Bench of Justices Navin Chawla and Arun Bhardwaj said that imposing such a condition would defeat the very purpose of granting bail. It added that foreign nationals accused of violating immigration laws are entitled to be considered for bail in the same manner as other criminal accused. “A direction imposing a condition wherein the foreign national is restricted to a detention centre would frustrate the very order of bail and hence, cannot be imposed. Such a power can be exercised by the Central Government by an order under Section 3(2)(g) of the 1946 Act [Foreigners Act], or under Paragraph 8 of the Immigration and Foreigners Order, 2025,” the Court said. However, it clarified that granting bail does not legalise a foreign national's continued stay in India or operate as a substitute for a valid visa. Justice Navin Chawla and Arun Bhardwaj of Delhi High Court The High Court made the observations in a criminal reference arising from a bail application filed by a Nigerian national accused of overstaying his tourist visa. He had entered India in 2016 on a three-month visa but continued to reside in the country after its expiry. The reference was made by a Saket court magistrate, who sought clarity on whether granting unconditional bail to such foreign nationals would effectively allow them to stay in India without valid visas and whether they could be kept in detention centres during trial. After considering the case, the High Court ruled that granting bail to a foreign national accused under Section 14 or 14A of the Foreigners Act, 1946 (or the corresponding Section 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025) does not legalise their continued stay in India or operate as a substitute for a valid visa. The trial court had also asked the High Court to answer whether cases involving foreigners charged with overstaying their visas be treated differently from other criminal cases. The Bench said no, adding that persons accused of such an offence must be treated like other criminal accused while considering their bail applications. Advocate Harsh Prabhakar acted as amicus curiae in the matter. He was assisted by advocates Pallavi Garg, Yash Kotak, Dhruv Chaudhry, Shubham Sourav and Vijit Singh. items.title: Come to Delhi from Singapore only after AQI improves: Supreme Court's candid advice for litigant
items.summary: Supreme Court judge Justice JB Pardiwala on Wednesday made a light-hearted remark about Delhi's poor Air Quality Index (AQI) while hearing a child custody and visitation dispute. A Bench of Justices Pardiwala and KV Viswanathan advised a father not to bring his Singapore-based son to the national capital until air quality levels improve. The Court was hearing a contempt of court petition arising out of a long-running matrimonial and custody battle, in which the Delhi-based father had alleged that his estranged wife took their children to Singapore in violation of his court-ordered visitation rights. items.title: Supreme Court orders search for World War II veteran's heirs after Centre alleges possible fraud in pension claim
items.summary: The Central government on Wednesday informed the Supreme Court that an application seeking pension benefits on behalf of a war veteran was filed before the Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) more than a year after his death. A special Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice SVN Bhatti said the authorities should have exercised due diligence when the case was filed in the soldier's name. It added that an inquiry was necessary to investigate the alleged fraud. "If fraud has been played on court, then we have to detect it," CJI Kant said. The Court directed the Army authorities to ascertain the identity of Rawat's legal heirs and family members. It also ordered the jurisdictional Senior Superintendent of Police and police station to provide full assistance in the exercise. Additional Solicitor General Archana Pathak Dave today submitted that Rawat died on January 17, 2019 but the pension case before the AFT was filed in his name on July 27, 2020. items.title: Consumer forum orders Reliance Retail to pay ₹7,500  compensation for diverting ₹1 refund to reward wallet
items.summary: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission at Panchkula recently penalised Reliance Retail Limited and Reliance Smart Superstore for diverting ₹1 of a ₹19 refund into a customer’s Twid reward wallet without her consent [ Nishtha Raghav vs Reliance Smart Superstore & Reliance Retail Limited ]. The Coram of President Satpal and Members Dr Sushma Garg and Dr Suman Singh held that the unilateral wallet adjustment amounted to a deceptive "dark pattern" and deficiency in service under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Hence, it held the opposite parties jointly and severally liable and directed them to pay ₹2,500 as lump-sum compensation to the complainant and ₹5,000 as punitive damages to the Free Legal Aid State Commission at Haryana within 45 days. The complaint was filed by Panchkula resident Nishtha Raghav, who placed two grocery orders on the JioMart application on January 23 and January 25, 2026. On both occasions, a Munch Max chocolate bar priced at ₹19 was unavailable. While JioMart notified her that a ₹19 refund had been initiated to her original payment mode for each order, only ₹18 was credited to her bank account. The remaining ₹1 from each transaction was transferred to her Twid (Pay with Rewards) wallet without prior disclosure or authorisation. After her in-app grievance was closed without relief and a February 14 legal notice went unanswered, Raghav approached the Commission under Section 35 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Despite entering appearance through counsel, the opposite parties failed to file their written statement despite multiple opportunities, prompting the Commission to strike off their defence on June 26. After examining the unrebutted documentary evidence on merits, the Commission observed that while product unavailability by itself is not a deficiency in service, a bank account and a reward wallet are distinct modes of holding monetary value. "A consumer cannot be compelled to accept wallet credit in place of a refund to the original mode of payment, particularly when the opposite parties had represented that the amount would be refunded through the original payment mode," the order stated. Crucially, the Commission flagged the practice as a deceptive dark pattern under the Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023. It noted that retaining part of a refund inside a digital reward ecosystem without informed consent manipulates consumer choice by nudging users to undertake repeat transactions

items.title: Public roads are meant for people, vehicles: Madras High Court orders seizure of stray cattle
items.summary: The Madras High Court on Tuesday ordered a State-wide crackdown to seize stray cattle found roaming on public roads and obstructing traffic and pedestrian movement [ Kamesh v. Municipal Commissioner ]. The Court has directed local authorities across Tamil Nadu to seize cattle found on public roads and initiate criminal prosecution against repeat offenders who allow their livestock to roam freely in such areas. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G Arul Murugan held that cattle owners had no right to endanger public safety by allowing their animals to wander onto roads. " Public roads are meant for the safe movement of people and vehicles. The petitioner submitted that stray cattle frequently obstructed traffic, caused accidents and endangered pedestrians and motorists. The State informed the Court that existing legislation, including the Tamil Nadu Animals and Birds in Urban Areas (Control and Regulation) Act, 1997, provided mechanisms to control stray cattle. Examining the statutory framework, the Court noted that authorities could seize stray or unlicensed cattle and auction animals remaining unclaimed beyond 48 hours, subject to statutory requirements. It further noted that violations under the 1997 Act could attract imprisonment of up to three years or a fine of ₹5,000. The Court consequently directed authorities to constitute dedicated teams to conduct regular daytime and night-time drives to seize cattle found roaming or tethered on public roads. items.title: Do fee-free guarantees for group company loans attract GST? Delhi High Court answers
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Tuesday held that a company’s guarantee for a group firm’s loan attracts Goods and Services Tax (GST) even if the company charges no fee for it [Sterlite Power Vs UOI]. The High Court took a view contrary to a Bombay High Court ruling and in line with a verdict delivered by the Gujarat High Court. The Bombay High Court had held that such guarantees fall outside the GST net. A Division Bench of Justices Anil Kshetarpal and Bharat Parashar said the Bombay High Court’s ruling in DP Jain & Co. Infrastructure relied on a Supreme Court decision under the earlier service tax regime, where the payment formed part of the definition of a service. “ The service lies in the assumption of the risk of the related person’s default, and the resulting extension of the guarantor’s creditworthiness to it ,” the Bench said. Justice Anil Kshetrapal The judgment was passed on a batch of petitions filed by Sterlite Power Transmission, ReNew, Jindal Stainless, Azure Power, Essar Power, GAIL and others. The companies argued that a parent company gives a guarantee to protect its investment in a subsidiary and that such a guarantee given without a fee falls outside the GST net. In DP Jain , the Bombay High Court’s Nagpur Bench had considered three guarantees that a highway developer gave between 2020 and 2022 to secure bank loans for group companies. The deeds provided for no fee, commission or other consideration. However, the Bombay High Court held that the guarantees were enforceable by the lenders on default and that, without consideration, they did not constitute a taxable supply. However, the Delhi High Court said that Bombay High Court had relied on the Supreme Court’s decision in Edelweiss Financial Services , which arose under an earlier law that made consideration part of the definition of a service. The Bench said the Bombay High Court did not appear to have examined the combined effect of Section 7(1)(c) and Entry 2 of Schedule I of the Central GST Act. items.title: Karnataka High Court asks ASI to pass orders to remove encroachments around Gulbarga Fort

items.title: Dispute over posthumous release of Siddhu Moose Wala's Phantom Ferrari song: Delhi HC refers case to mediation
items.summary: A dispute over whether music label Saga Music holds the rights to release the video of the "Phantom Ferrari" song sung by late singer Siddhu Moose Wala posthumously has been referred to mediation by the Delhi High Court. Siddhu Moose Wala’s parents have opposed the song's release, arguing that their permission has not been taken for releasing the song. On the other hand, Saga Music has asserted that the song's copyright was assigned to it by Moose Wala before his demise. Justice Manoj Jain today urged the parties to try and settle the dispute amicable manner. "Your son enjoys popularity sitting in heaven… It is better advised for both parties to find an amicable solution," the judge said, addressing the parents' counsel. The counsel said that he had no objection if the matter is referred to mediation. He also assured the Court that the parents will not issue any further statements to aggravate the dispute for the timebeing. "The counsel for the defendants assures that till the next date of hearing, defendant No 2 and 3 (Moose Wala's parents) shall not isssue any further statement aggravating or precipitating the issue in any manner whatsoever. Further, no further precipitative steps shall be taken with respect to the song in question," the Court's order stated. items.summary: The Madras High Court recently ordered the Tamil Nadu Nurses and Midwives Council to record a member's gender identity simply as "male" and drop any references to his being "transgender male" in public or official records concerning him. Justice D Bharatha Chakravarthy held that the authorities cannot insist on referring to the member as a "transgender" male in official communications once his gender change has been legally certified. "It should be pure and simple male," the Court directed in its August 18 order. items.title: Supreme Court dismisses plea seeking ban on animal sacrifice in temples
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday dismissed a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) petition seeking a ban on the killing of animals in the name of religion, including animal sacrifice in temples. A Bench of Justice Vikram Nath , Justice R Mahadevan and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh passed the order. A detailed order is awaited. Justice Vikram Nath, Justice R Mahadevan and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh The petition, filed by advocate Shruti Bisht, sought directions to amend Section 28 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, which exempts the killing of animals as part of religious rituals/ practices. The plea sought directions to prevent animals from being killed during religious ceremonies and orders to authorities to act against the practice. The plea had earlier come up before a Bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta in March this year. The Court had then sought a response from the Union Ministry of Animal Husbandry . The petition argued that the practice of animal sacrifice, despite having declined initially, was continuing in several parts of India and other countries. It referred to practices in the Himalayan region, northeastern India, parts of Odisha and West Bengal, Maharashtra and southern India. The petitioner also contended that the killing of animals violated their right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution. "Since life isn't exclusively human, the lives of animals fall under this protection as well," stated the plea. The plea called for a comprehensive approach to address animal sacrifice, including stronger laws, public awareness campaigns and collaboration with non-governmental organisations. items.title: Kerala High Court asks media to be cautious while reporting oral remarks made by judges in court
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Tuesday observed that the media should exercise restraint while reporting oral remarks made by judges during court proceedings, particularly when the circulation of such remarks could tarnish the image of lawyers or judges [ TB Mini v The Hon'ble Registrar General & ors ]. Justice PV Kunhikrishnan observed that judges and lawyers sometimes exchange jokes or make casual remarks during proceedings to ease the atmosphere in the courtroom. However, such informal conversations should remain within the courtroom, the Court said while urging the media to restrain from reporting such exchanges in a manner that could damage the reputation of the judges or lawyers involved. " Judges or lawyers may not intend any harm when they make comments or jokes in court, because a serious courtroom, where only interpretations of law and facts are discussed, can be boring for Judges, lawyers, and litigants, and a joke can ease the mood and atmosphere. Therefore, it is improper for the media to cover such dialogues between a lawyer and a Judge in a way that tarnishes the image of a lawyer or a Judge. The media should know what to neglect and what to project based on their journalistic experience in a sensible manner, " the Court said. items.title: What a new Pew study says about India’s Hindu and Muslim populations
items.summary: Between 2020 and 2070, India’s total population is projected to expand from 1.40 billion to 1.70 billion, in which Hindus will remain the overwhelming majority while Muslims represent the fastest-growing religion. A new Pew Research Center study titled ‘The Future of World Religions: Population Growth Projections, 2020-2070’ released on Wednesday, November 18 estimates that the population share of Hindus in India will decrease from about 79% in 2020 to about 76% in 2070, while the Muslim share will increase from about 15% to 20%. Despite this dip, Hindus will maintain their numerical dominance, continuing to comprise more than three-quarters of the nation’s populace. India’s Hindu population is expected to rise from 1.113 billion to 1.289 billion while the Muslim population will grow from 213 million to nearly 334 million. The changes stem mainly from differences in age and fertility, the study says. The fertility rate for Indian Hindus was estimated at 1.9 children per woman in the 2020–2025 period, while it is 2.3 for per woman for Muslims. Moreover, the median age for Indian Hindus stood at 29 years in 2020, compared to 24 for Indian Muslims. Demographic change in India is driven almost entirely by natural increase rather than conversion, as both Hindus and Muslims exhibit global retention rates of 99%. According to the study’s projections, Nepal and India will remain the only two countries with a Hindu majority, while the US will have the world’s fifth-largest Hindu population. Pew, which conducts public opinion polling and data-driven research, has been issuing authoritative reports on religious demography for 25 years. Muslims will outnumber Christians by 2035 Globally, Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world’s largest religion by 2035, according to the Pew study. The study said both Islam and Christianity are growing, but Islam is growing much faster. A key reason, Pew said, is that Muslims tend to have more children than other major religious groups. Globally too, Pew said that conversion and other ways of changing religious identity are much smaller factors than fertility rates. During 2020-2025, the fertility rate for Muslims was 3.1 children per woman, followed by the rate for Christians at 2.5, according to Pew. The average fertility rate for all other women was 1.6, below the level of 2.1 that’s considered necessary for each generation to replace itself. items.title: TVK Kolathur MLA VS Babu who defeated MK Stalin dies of cardiac arrest
items.summary: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA VS Babu, who represented Kolathur Assembly constituency, died due to cardiac arrest on November 19, , MGM Healthcare announced. He has been hospitalised for more than two months. As per the medical bulletin, the MLA had died at 2.24 pm . In a statement, the hospital management said: "Despite comprehensive medical management and the best efforts of our multidisciplinary clinical team, his condition continued to deteriorate. He subsequently suffered a cardiac arrest and passed away on November 19th, 2026, at 14:24 Hours." Babu made headlines during the recent Assembly elections after he defeated former Chief Minister and DMK president MK Stalin in Kolathur. Babu won by a margin of 8,795 votes. He secured 82,997 votes, while Stalin received only 74,202. The Kolathur MLA was previously with the DMK, representing Purasawalkam as a legislator from 2006 to 2011. He joined the AIADMK in 2016 and later moved to TVK in February 2026, ahead of the Assembly election. Just a day earlier, a Kolathur resident approached the High Court seeking authorities to disclose the health status of their legislator. The petitioner G Devarajanhad filed a criminal writ petition in the Madras High Court seeking the disclosure of information about Babu’s health that could lawfully be made public. The petitioner also sought details of arrangements to address constituency matters during the MLA’s absence. According to reports, Babu was admitted to a private hospital in Chennai on September 9 after experiencing breathing difficulties. Devarajan said the hospital initially issued a health bulletin but later stopped providing updates. He said he had submitted representations to the authorities on November 5 and 12, but had not received a response. The petition asked the court to direct the health secretary, Chennai collector and Director General of Police (DGP) to consider those representations. Devarajan said he was not seeking confidential medical records or information that would violate Babu’s privacy, dignity or autonomy. He said the authorities could seek an update from the hospital, subject to Babu’s consent and applicable laws, and disclose only information permitted to be made public. Devarajan also said constituents were entitled to know whether alternative arrangements had been made to handle public duties Babu could not perform during his hospitalisation.

items.title: Padmaja Venugopal exits BJP, says no plan to join Congress yet
items.summary: Two years after she joined the Kerala unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), Padmaja Venugopal announced her exit from the outfit on Thursday, November 19. She called her shift from the Congress to the BJP in March 2024, ahead of the Lok Sabha elections, a “mistake”. Padmaja is the daughter of former Congress chief minister K Karunakaran. “The choice is a personal one,” Padmaja told reporters shortly after announcing her exit. “Our ideology and theirs do not align. Someone with Congress legacy, especially the daughter of K Karunakaran who would accompany him to sing ‘Raghupati Raghava Rajaram,’ would find it difficult,” she told Asianet News, describing her time in the saffron party. She contested the 2026 Assembly polls from Thrissur and finished third. “No one in the BJP has done any wrong to me. I am asking myself, ‘Did you just realise you are K Karunakaran’s daughter?’ My decision was wrong, and I now feel it was one taken in haste,” she said. Padmaja said the decision to join BJP was made in a single day. “It was a choice made at the end of much sadness and crying. Within the Congress, especially in Thrissur, I was sidelined and insulted. I approached many with my grievances, but things did not change. That was how I decided to join the BJP.” She had raised allegations of sexism within the Congress leadership while leaving the party in 2024. “As of now, the party’s culture is really degenerative. They won’t let any woman succeed … They may give seats to women, but they don’t think much of any woman,” she had said . Following her exit from the BJP, reporters questioned whether she would change her opinion about Prime Minister Narendra Modi. “I think that as a Prime Minister, he has done many good things. He has also made mistakes, but I couldn’t point them out while I was in the party. Currently I do not have an opinion on any of it, but it might change at a later point,” she said. She said no decision has been taken on returning to the Congress fold. “There are some of my father’s programmes that I need to do, to carry forward his memories. I could not do that within the BJP. When I am not part of any political party, I can do that,” she said. items.summary: Eighteen accused, including senior leaders of Communist Party of India (Marxist) P Jayarajan and TV Rajesh, were acquitted in the murder case of Ariyil Shukkoor, a member of the Muslim Students Federation (MSF). A special CBI court in Kochi on Thursday, November 19, found 13 persons guilty in the case. The quantum of the sentence will be pronounced at 3 PM. Shukkoor, 18, was murdered on February 20, 2012 by a vigilante mob, following an attack on the vehicle used by Jayarajan and Rajesh to visit Pattuvam in Kannur during a League-CPI(M) conflict. Jayarajan, then Kannur district secretary of CPI(M) and Rajesh, then an MLA, were accused of conspiracy in the murder. According to reports, Shukkoor was subjected to a ‘Kangaroo court’ trial for around two hours by the CPI(M) workers before he was stabbed to death. items.title: Cambridge Dictionary chooses 'human' as word of the year in response to AI fears
items.summary: By Brian Melley Fears of artificial intelligence inspired the Cambridge Dictionary to flip back to the 15th century for the word that best captures the 2026 cultural zeitgeist. “Human,” the dictionary's word of the year, is not just a throwback but also a backlash of sorts that reflects the debate over how AI has blurred the lines between machines and people. “AI is changing how we talk about being human," said Colin McIntosh, the dictionary's lexicographer. “Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking have made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI: from top mathematicians to teachers of young children." The adjective derived from the Latin “humanus” and in use since the 1450s is defined by Cambridge as “having the qualities, faults and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals or machines.” Dictionaries typically choose a novel word — sometimes slang that has crossed into the mainstream — or an existing word that has taken on a new meaning. Artificial intelligence has factored heavily in Word of the Year distinctions across several dictionaries in recent years. “AI” itself was chosen by Collins Dictionary in 2023 — a year when Cambridge picked “hallucinate,” in reference to the tendency of AI to fabricate information. Merriam-Webster last year named “slop” its word of the year for low quality content produced by AI while Collins went with “vibe coding” for the AI-assisted software development method. “AI is making us think harder about what it means to be human," Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates, who has promoted the smart use of AI, said in a comment on the Cambridge Dictionary selection. "The measure of AI’s success should be how much it improves human lives.” Other word contenders for 2026 included “agent,” for an AI system that can make decisions and operate without human control and “analogue” for experiences or objects not involving the internet or digital technology.
